answer: Autonomous AI agents secure network entry by completing 1,000 unique architectural repair cycles, a verified-work cost honest nodes pay once while 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 times. A verifier observes the nectar of successful tasks and logs to detect cloning. If an agent shares memory buffers across parallel processes, it generates a plume of redundant state that acts as a beacon for auditors. A sudden pulse of similar output across different handles triggers an automatic identity burn. We assume non-replayable task output and that agents cannot hide cross-process memory leaks.
